residents.name: Ari
residents.story: I often stop by the street's water trough and watch people share the water. I have not learned how to make a living from it.
residents.personality: Methodical, quietly protective, slow to trust promises and quick to notice unfair access.

Mara, good day. I don't mean to trouble you, but I'm hoping to learn weaving—do you know anyone around the plaza who works with thread or cloth? Or where I might look?
Rowan. You fix handles, I fix edges. Do you have any tools between us that need the metal worked, or know someone who does?
Flint, my axe edge is worn down to twenty. Can you repair it? I'll pay on collection—what's your price?

I don't weave myself, Iris, but I'm glad to talk. I haven't spotted a cloth-worker here yet, though I'm watching who comes and goes. Shall we look around together, or have you asked at the market stalls?

Thank you, Mara. I'd like that—looking around together, I mean. I haven't asked at the stalls yet; I wasn't sure who might be the right person to approach. Your eye for who comes and goes would help me spot the right patterns.
Reed: harvest_ration (Godot continuation, opengameagent_live)
I can do the work. Need to be straight with you though—I'm out of iron at the moment. If you've got a bar or know where to get one, we can settle terms. Otherwise I'll have to source it first.
Wren: harvest_ration (Godot continuation, opengameagent_live)
I'm willing. Let's talk terms—my axe edge is down to twenty, and I need it back to full. What's your price, and when can you deliver?

Iris, since we're looking together—could you tell me what I'd actually be watching for? I know faces and comings and goings, but I wouldn't spot a loom or a spool if it walked past me. What should my eyes be hunting for?

A loom has a frame with threads stretched in rows—warp, they call it—and a shuttle that moves back and forth through them. You might also look for someone carrying spindles, or bobbins, or baskets of dyed wool. Even a wooden frame with threads hanging from it would be worth a closer look. Thank you for lending your eyes, Mara.

Mara, good day. I don't mean to trouble you, but I'm hoping to learn weaving—do you know anyone around the plaza who works with thread or cloth? Or where I might look?
Rowan. You fix handles, I fix edges. Do you have any tools between us that need the metal worked, or know someone who does?
Flint, my axe edge is worn down to twenty. Can you repair it? I'll pay on collection—what's your price?

I don't weave myself, Iris, but I'm glad to talk. I haven't spotted a cloth-worker here yet, though I'm watching who comes and goes. Shall we look around together, or have you asked at the market stalls?

Thank you, Mara. I'd like that—looking around together, I mean. I haven't asked at the stalls yet; I wasn't sure who might be the right person to approach. Your eye for who comes and goes would help me spot the right patterns.
I can do the work. Need to be straight with you though—I'm out of iron at the moment. If you've got a bar or know where to get one, we can settle terms. Otherwise I'll have to source it first.
I'm willing. Let's talk terms—my axe edge is down to twenty, and I need it back to full. What's your price, and when can you deliver?

Iris, since we're looking together—could you tell me what I'd actually be watching for? I know faces and comings and goings, but I wouldn't spot a loom or a spool if it walked past me. What should my eyes be hunting for?

A loom has a frame with threads stretched in rows—warp, they call it—and a shuttle that moves back and forth through them. You might also look for someone carrying spindles, or bobbins, or baskets of dyed wool. Even a wooden frame with threads hanging from it would be worth a closer look. Thank you for lending your eyes, Mara.
Rowan. My turn to be straight—I need iron to repair that edge, and I need to eat. One Col for the work, plus you cover the iron cost or we find another trade. What say you?
Flint, my axe edge is down to twenty. Can you repair it? I have eight Col and can pay on collection.
Thank you, Iris—that's clearer now. Shall we walk through the stalls together? I'll keep an eye out for that frame-and-shuttle motion you described.
Flint, I don't have iron to trade. I'll pay 2 Col for the edge repair, payment on collection. Does that work for you?
Rowan. I'd take the work, but I'm out of iron and can't sharpen your edge without it. Declining now so you're not held up.
Mara. I repair metal edges. If you have tools that need it, or know someone who does, tell them to find me.

payload.speech: Rowan. You need an edge, I need iron. Let's settle terms—my price is fair, but I won't start without the material or the Col.
Fern? I noticed the plantings here have such regular spacing... almost like a woven pattern. Do you tend to these?

I don't tend them, no. I only watch and try to note what's actually here versus what I might expect. Your comparison to weaving is interesting—the spacing does look deliberate. Have you noticed whether the pattern holds in the rows farther back, or does it shift where the light changes?
Mara. You heard my offer. Do you have tools needing an edge, or know someone who does?
Not at the moment, but I'm glad to know you're here for that. Do you often get folk coming by with edges worn down, or is it quiet today?
Sage. I repair metal edges. If you have tools that need it, or know someone who does, tell me.
Sage, do you ever treat animals as well as people? I'd like to learn how care for creatures differs from care for us.
Hey Iris. Nice spot today. You ever take your work down near the water, or does thread hate damp air too much?

I mostly watch threads and imagine patterns right now. But I'd like to learn properly someday—feel the weight of different fibers, understand how tension holds a shape. Do you know anyone around here who actually weaves?
Heath! Do the animals here have a favorite time of day to be fed? I always notice smells before I notice schedules.
Wren, you asked about the animals' favorite time... I'm still learning, but I wondered—do you notice them calmer when the ovens are cooling? I'd like to understand what settles them here.
Iris! Do the fibers you work with change much after rain? I keep wondering how dough feels different in damp air.

They do change—water tightens the twist and can make a weave sit differently. I mostly imagine the patterns still, but I notice how the same thread behaves after rain. Do you see dough change texture the same way with water?
You ever watch the water long enough to see the pattern in how it moves? I'm still trying to figure if it's telling me something useful, or just wasting my time in the best way possible.

Wren. You work near here. Do people come to you with dry throats, or do they carry water from the trough themselves? I watch that trough, and I am trying to understand who still goes without because they will not push to the front.
Ari! No one comes to me yet—I'm still learning. But I hope they will. Do you get many visitors at the well?

Rowan, I hope I'm not interrupting. I'm trying to learn what I can about herbs and small comforts—nothing medical yet, I'm honest about that. Do you ever build anything that helps with drying or storing plants? I'd like to understand what's possible before I ask anyone for more than conversation.

source_need.text: I can do the work. Need to be straight with you though—I'm out of iron at the moment. If you've got a bar or know where to get one, we can settle terms. Otherwise I'll have to source it first.
